_comment: Mutation testing asks the question coverage cannot: are the assertions real? Stryker changes production code — flips a boolean, drops a call, swaps an operator — and a test suite that stays green against the change was never proving that line. Scoped to one domain on purpose: git is where a wrong guard loses a user's work, and at 84% statement coverage it is exactly where coverage might be lying. Widen the `mutate` glob only with a measured runtime to justify it.
_plugins: pnpm's nested store defeats Stryker's default '@stryker-mutator/*' plugin glob; name the runner so it resolves from the sandbox.
_ignore: Stryker copies the project into a sandbox. `.claude/skills/*` are symlinks to directories (the vendor-neutral .agents tree), which the copy cannot follow, and none of these affect a mutant's outcome.
_thresholds: Today's measured score for the committed scope, rounded down. It may rise; it may not fall. Raise the floor when the domain improves — never lower it to make a run green.
_tempDir: Absolute, outside the repo. A sandbox under the working tree is a full mirror of the project, and every lint script that walks the tree then scans the copy — a leftover sandbox failed the architecture ceiling and the docs gate on files that are not really there.
